segments.arabic: [632] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن أبيه عن حفص بن عاصم عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة قال
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from his father, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ برجل
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man.

segments.arabic: قال وحدثني عبد الرحمن قال: حدثنا بهز بن أسد قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني سعد بن إبراهيم قال: سمعت حفص بن عاصم قال: سمعت رجلا من الأزد يقال له مالك بن بحينة
segments.english: He said: And ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me. He said: Bahz ibn Asad related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed me. He said: I heard Hafs ibn ‘Asim say: I heard a man from al-Azd called Malik ibn Buhaynah say:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى رجلا وقد أقيمت الصلاة يصلي ركعتين فلما انصرف رسول الله ﷺ لاث به الناس، وقال له رسول الله ﷺ الصبح أربعا الصبح أربعا
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man praying two rak‘ahs when the iqamah had been given. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, the people gathered around him, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “The dawn prayer as four? The dawn prayer as four?”

segments.arabic: تابعه غندر ومعاذ عن شعبة في مالك، وقال ابن إسحاق عن سعد عن حفص عن عبد الله بن بحينة، وقال حماد أخبرنا سعد عن حفص عن مالك
segments.english: Ghundar and Mu‘adh corroborated it from Shu‘bah concerning Malik. And Ibn Ishaq said: From Sa‘d, from Hafs, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Buhaynah. And Hammad said: Sa‘d informed us, from Hafs, from Malik.

notes: Both full opening routes, the first route’s brief opening, the repeated dawn-prayer question and all three closing transmission notes remain. The selected source names ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah in the first route, Malik ibn Buhaynah in the second, ‘Abd Allah ibn Buhaynah in Ibn Ishaq’s note and Malik in Hammad’s note. These forms are not harmonized. Ibn Hajar discusses the naming discrepancy and the maternal name; the English comparisons abbreviate the routes and closing notes.

The digital source and historical print say concerning Malik in the Ghundar/Mu‘adh note; the modern print has from Malik. The pronoun in people gathered around him remains unexpanded: Ibn Hajar explicitly records competing antecedents. The English does not settle the pronoun through an inserted name. Brill 171 contains the beginning of the chain, continued on 172.

segments.arabic: [633] حدثنا عمر بن حفص بن غياث قال: حدثني أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن إبراهيم قال الأسود قال
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Ibrahim, who said: Al-Aswad said:

segments.arabic: كنا عند عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فذكرنا المواظبة على الصلاة والتعظيم لها قالت لما مرض رسول الله ﷺ مرضه الذي مات فيه فحضرت الصلاة فأذن، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فقيل له إن أبا بكر رجل أسيف إذا قام في مقامك لم يستطع أن يصلي بالناس وأعاد فأعادوا له فأعاد الثالثة، فقال إنكن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فخرج أبو بكر فصلى فوجد النبي ﷺ من نفسه خفة فخرج يهادي بين رجلين كأني أنظر إلى رجليه تخطان من الوجع فأراد أبو بكر أن يتأخر فأومأ إليه النبي ﷺ أن مكانك ثم أتي به حتى جلس إلى جنبه
segments.english: We were with ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and we mentioned constancy in prayer and the great regard due to it. She said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, the time for prayer came and the adhan was given. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” He was told: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He repeated it, and they repeated it to him. He repeated it a third time and said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr went out and prayed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out supported between two men. It is as though I can see his feet dragging from the pain. Abu Bakr wanted to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Then he was brought until he sat beside him.

segments.arabic: قيل للأعمش وكان النبي ﷺ يصلي وأبو بكر يصلي بصلاته والناس يصلون بصلاة أبي بكر، فقال برأسه نعم
segments.english: Al-A‘mash was asked: “Was the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying, with Abu Bakr praying following his prayer, and the people praying following Abu Bakr’s prayer?” He nodded yes.

segments.arabic: رواه أبو داود عن شعبة عن الأعمش بعضه وزاد أبو معاوية جلس عن يسار أبي بكر فكان أبو بكر يصلي قائما
segments.english: Abu Dawud related part of it from Shu‘bah, from al-A‘mash. Abu Mu‘awiyah added: “He sat to Abu Bakr’s left, and Abu Bakr prayed standing.”

notes: The selected father related to me agrees with the modern print; the historical print uses related to us. Aishah’s full selected honorific is retained. The repeated request and reply, third instruction, support by two men, feet dragging in pain and gesture to stay remain. The question to al-A‘mash and his affirmative nod are separately visible, as are Abu Dawud’s partial route through Shu‘bah and Abu Mu‘awiyah’s additional left-side/standing detail. The English comparisons omit or abbreviate Abu Dawud’s route; it is not dropped.

segments.arabic: [634] حدثنا إبراهيم بن موسى قال: أخبرنا هشام بن يوسف عن معمر عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله قال: قالت عائشة
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me. He said: ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: لما ثقل النبي ﷺ واشتد وجعه استأذن أزواجه أن يمرض في بيتي فأذن له فخرج بين رجلين تخط رجلاه الأرض وكان بين العباس ورجل آخر
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and his pain intensified, he asked his wives’ permission to be cared for in my house, and they gave him permission. He went out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. He was between al-‘Abbas and another man.

segments.arabic: قال عبيد الله فذكرت ذلك لابن عباس ما قالت عائشة، فقال لي وهل تدري من الرجل الذي لم تسم عائشة قلت لا قال هو علي بن أبي طالب
segments.english: ‘Ubayd Allah said: I mentioned to Ibn ‘Abbas what ‘A’ishah had said. He said to me: “Do you know who the man was whom ‘A’ishah did not name?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib.”

notes: The wives’ permission, Aishah’s house, two supporting men and feet dragging remain. ‘Ali is identified only in the later conversation between ‘Ubayd Allah and Ibn ‘Abbas, presented separately; his name is not inserted into Aishah’s account. The historical print adds an honorific after ‘Ali that is absent from the selected digital and modern texts; it is not imported.

segments.arabic: [635] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘:

segments.arabic: ان ابن عمر إذن بالصلاة في ليلة ذات برد وريح، ثم قال ألا صلوا في الرحال، ثم قال إن رسول الله ﷺ كان يأمر المؤذن إذا كانت ليلة ذات برد ومطر يقول ألا صلوا في الرحال
segments.english: That Ibn ‘Umar gave the adhan for prayer on a cold, windy night. Then he said: “Listen, pray in your dwellings.” Then he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to instruct the caller, when it was a cold, rainy night, to say: ‘Listen, pray in your dwellings.’”

notes: The first night is cold and windy; the instruction in the second part concerns a cold and rainy night. Both attention particles and the repeated dwellings instruction remain. The digital إذن is retained in the original Arabic; both inspected prints read أذن with the adhan sense confirmed by context and both English comparisons. This orthographic difference is recorded, not silently rewritten.

segments.arabic: [636] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن ابن شهاب عن محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari:

segments.arabic: أن عتبان بن مالك كان يؤم قومه وهو أعمى وأنه قال لرسول الله ﷺ يا رسول الله إنها تكون الظلمة والسيل وأنا رجل ضرير البصر فصل يا رسول الله في بيتي مكانا أتخذه مصلى فجاءه رسول الله ﷺ، فقال أين تحب أن أصلي فأشار إلى مكان من البيت فصلى فيه رسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: That ‘Itban ibn Malik used to lead his people in prayer, and he was blind. He said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Messenger of Allah, there is darkness and floodwater, and I am a man with impaired sight. Pray, Messenger of Allah, in a place in my house that I can take as a place of prayer.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: “Where would you like me to pray?” He pointed to a place in the house, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed there.

notes: The full chain retains Malik related to me. ‘Itban’s leading his people, blindness, darkness and floodwater, request for a particular place in the house, the question about his preference and the eventual prayer there remain. All three selected honorifics remain; the English comparison’s additional introductory eyesight sentence is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [637] حدثنا عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد قال: حدثنا عبد الحميد صاحب الزيادي قال: سمعت عبد الله بن الحارث قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith say:

segments.arabic: خطبنا بن عباس في يوم ذي ردغ فأمر المؤذن لما بلغ حي على الصلاة قال قل الصلاة في الرحال فنظر بعضهم إلى بعض فكأنهم أنكروا، فقال: كانكم أنكرتم هذا إن هذا فعله من هو خير مني يعني النبي ﷺ إنها عزمة وإني كرهت أن أحرجكم
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas addressed us on a muddy day. When the caller reached “Come to prayer,” he instructed him, saying: “Say: ‘Prayer in the dwellings.’” Some of them looked at one another, as though they disapproved. He said: “It seems that you disapprove of this. Someone better than me did this”—meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. “It is a binding duty, and I disliked putting you in hardship.”

segments.arabic: وعن حماد عن عاصم عن عبد الله بن الحارث عن ابن عباس نحوه غير أنه قال كرهت أن أؤثمكم فتجيئون تدوسون الطين إلى ركبكم
segments.english: And from Hammad, from ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn ‘Abbas, something similar, except that he said: “I disliked causing you to incur sin, so that you would come trudging through mud up to your knees.”

notes: The first Hammad route retains ‘Abd al-Hamid’s association with al-Ziyadi and the full ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith chain. The instruction at Come to prayer, mutual looks, disapproval, better-than-me comparison and source’s Prophet aside remain. The second complete Hammad/‘Asim route and its distinct wording about sin and mud to the knees remain separately visible. The first wording concerns hardship, the second causing sin; they are not harmonized. Binding duty renders the selected عزمة without appending a new ruling.

segments.arabic: [638] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة قال:
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said:

segments.arabic: سألت أبا سعيد الخدري، فقال
segments.english: I asked Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, and he said:

segments.arabic: جاءت سحابة فمطرت حتى سال السقف وكان من جريد النخل فأقيمت الصلاة فرأيت رسول الله ﷺ يسجد في الماء والطين حتى رأيت أثر الطين في جبهته
segments.english: A cloud came and rained until the roof leaked. It was made of palm fronds. The iqamah was given, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in the water and mud, until I saw the mark of mud on his forehead.

notes: Both inspected prints have سال السقف, meaning that the roof leaked; the digital text has سأل السقف. Only this spelling is corrected, through a recorded two-print correction and visible notice with the original preserved. Abu Salamah’s question is retained separately and attributed before Abu Sa‘id’s reply; the comparisons begin directly with the reply. The palm-frond roof, iqamah, water and mud, and mark on the forehead remain.

segments.arabic: [639] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا أنس بن سيرين قال: سمعت أنسا يقول:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said: I heard Anas say:

segments.arabic: قال رجل من الأنصار إني لا أستطيع الصلاة معك وكان رجلا ضخما فصنع للنبي ﷺ طعاما فدعاه إلى منزله فبسط له حصيرا ونضح طرف الحصير صلى عليه ركعتين،
segments.english: A man of the Ansar said: “I am unable to pray with you.” He was a large man. He prepared food for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and invited him to his house. He spread a mat for him and sprinkled water on the edge of the mat. He prayed two rak‘ahs on it.

segments.arabic: فقال رجل من آل الجارود لأنس أكان النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى قال: ما رأيته صلاها إلا يومئذ
segments.english: A man from the family of al-Jarud said to Anas: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha?” He said: “I never saw him pray it except on that day.”

notes: Anas ibn Sirin’s hearing from Anas remains. The man’s inability to pray with the addressee, his large build, food invitation, spread mat, sprinkled edge and two rak‘ahs remain. The separate question from a man of al-Jarud’s family and Anas’s limited eyewitness answer are not hidden or converted into a general claim.

segments.arabic: [640] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن هشام قال: حدثني أبي قال: سمعت عائشة عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father related to me. He said: I heard ‘A’ishah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

segments.arabic: إذا وضع العشاء وأقيمت الصلاة فابدؤوا بالعشاء
segments.english: “When supper is set out and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper.”

notes: Hisham’s father related to me and I heard ‘Aishah both remain in the full chain. The report contains supper and the iqamah; it does not name a specific obligatory prayer. The unnumbered chapter material is preserved separately and is excluded from the report and its eventual spoken script.

segments.arabic: [641] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا قدم العشاء فابدؤوا به قبل أن تصلوا صلاة المغرب ولا تعجلوا عن عشائكم
segments.english: “When supper is served, begin with it before you pray the Maghrib prayer, and do not hurry away from your supper.”

notes: The full al-Layth/‘Uqayl/Ibn Shihab/Anas chain remains. This report explicitly names Maghrib, unlike 640. Before praying Maghrib and not hurrying away from supper are both retained.

segments.arabic: [642] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل عن أبي أسامة عن عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا وضع عشاء أحدكم وأقيمت الصلاة فابدؤوا بالعشاء ولا يعجل حتى يفرغ منه
segments.english: “When supper is set out for one of you and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper, and he should not hurry until he has finished it.”

segments.arabic: وكان ابن عمر يوضع له الطعام وتقام الصلاة فلا يأتيها حتى يفرغ وإنه ليسمع قراءة الإمام،
segments.english: Food would be set out for Ibn ‘Umar and the iqamah would be given, but he would not go to it until he had finished, while he could hear the imam reciting.

segments.arabic: وقال زهير ووهب بن عثمان عن موسى بن عقبة عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: And Zuhayr and Wahb ibn ‘Uthman said: From Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا كان أحدكم على الطعام فلا يعجل حتى يقضي حاجته منه وإن أقيمت الصلاة
segments.english: “When one of you is eating, he should not hurry until he has satisfied his need for it, even if the iqamah has been given.”

segments.arabic: رواه إبراهيم بن المنذر عن وهب بن عثمان ووهب مديني
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related it from Wahb ibn ‘Uthman, and Wahb is from Madinah.

notes: The first saying, Ibn ‘Umar’s practice, complete Zuhayr/Wahb route and second saying, and Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir’s final route with Wahb’s Madinan identity remain in source order. Ibn ‘Umar actually hearing the imam is retained; it is not changed to a hypothetical even if. The modern print numbers the additional route 674, while the selected source and historical grouping keep it in this report. Bewley abbreviates the final route to another isnad and the Khan-family comparison omits it; the selected source is complete. The historical print introduces the closing note with Abu ‘Abd Allah said, absent from the selected digital and modern readings.

segments.arabic: [643] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم عن صالح عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني جعفر بن عمرو بن أمية أن أباه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ja‘far ibn ‘Amr ibn Umayyah informed me that his father said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يأكل ذراعا يحتز منها فدعي إلى الصلاة فقام فطرح السكين فصلى ولم يتوضأ
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, eating a foreleg, cutting pieces from it. He was called to prayer, so he stood up, put down the knife and prayed without performing ablution.

notes: Ja‘far’s father remains unnamed in the selected chain, which retains informed me. The selected ذراعا is rendered foreleg; neither the comparisons’ shoulder wording nor the Khan-family insertion of sheep is imported. Cutting pieces, being called, standing, setting down the knife and praying without ablution remain.

segments.arabic: [644] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا الحكم عن إبراهيم عن الأسود قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, who said:

segments.arabic: سألت عائشة ما كان النبي ﷺ يصنع في بيته قالت كان يكون في مهنة أهله تعني خدمة أهله فإذا حضرت الصلاة خرج إلى الصلاة
segments.english: I asked ‘A’ishah: “What did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do in his house?” She said: “He would be occupied in his family’s work”—meaning serving his family—“and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to prayer.”

notes: Al-Aswad’s question remains visible, followed by Aishah’s reply. The source’s explanatory aside meaning serving his family is retained explicitly within the report, without treating it as a new prophetic saying. The transition when prayer time came remains.

segments.arabic: [645] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا وهيب قال: حدثنا أيوب عن أبي قلابة قال
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

segments.arabic: جاءنا مالك بن الحويرث في مسجدنا هذا، فقال إني لأصلي بكم وما أريد الصلاة أصلي كيف رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي
segments.english: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith came to us in this mosque of ours and said: “I am indeed leading you in prayer, but prayer is not my purpose. I pray as I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray.”

segments.arabic: فقلت لأبي قلابة كيف كان يصلي قال مثل شيخنا هذا قال: وكان شيخا يجلس إذا رفع رأسه من السجود قبل أن ينهض في الركعة الأولى
segments.english: I said to Abu Qilabah: “How did he pray?” He said: “Like this elder of ours.” He said: He was an elderly man who would sit when he raised his head from prostration, before standing up in the first rak‘ah.

notes: The selected negative wording about intending prayer is retained. Bewley smooths the wording and the Khan-family comparison supplies a longer teaching explanation. Ibn Hajar discusses the motive and quotes an additional clause in another route; that additional clause is not inserted into this selected report. A separate context note flags this wording for independent review.

The follow-up question to Abu Qilabah and answer about their elder remain visible. The digital and modern print say he was an elderly man; the historical print says the elder. The sitting occurs after raising the head from prostration and before standing in the first rak‘ah. No elder’s name is imported from commentary.

segments.arabic: [646] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا حسين عن زائدة عن عبد الملك بن عمير قال: حدثني أبو بردة عن أبي موسى قال
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from Za’idah, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, who said: Abu Burdah related to me, from Abu Musa, who said:

segments.arabic: مرض النبي ﷺ فاشتد مرضه، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس قالت عائشة إنه رجل رقيق إذا قام مقامك لم يستطيع أن يصلي بالناس قال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فعادت، فقال مري أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فإنكن صواحب يوسف فأتاه الرسول فصلى بالناس في حياة النبي ﷺ
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill, and his illness grew severe. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “He is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” She repeated it, and he said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. You are the women associated with Yusuf.” The messenger came to him, and he led the people in prayer during the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The selected account begins with the Prophet’s illness and ends with prayer during his lifetime, retaining both honorifics, all three instructions and the repeated objection. The messenger coming to Abu Bakr is retained, although the Bewley comparison omits it. The full chain retains Abu Burdah related to me. The digital grammatical spelling يستطيع differs from the prints يستطع; the selected Arabic remains unchanged.

segments.arabic: [647] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها أنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that she said:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال في مرضه مروا أبا بكر يصلي بالناس قالت عائشة قلت: إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس فقالت عائشة فقلت لحفصة قولي له إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس ففعلت حفصة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: مه إنكن لأنتن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل للناس فقالت حفصة لعائشة ما كنت لأصيب منك خيرا
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said: “If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said to Hafsah: “Say to him: ‘If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.’” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Stop! You are indeed the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to ‘A’ishah: “I was never to get any good from you.”

notes: Mother of the Believers and Aishah’s complete selected honorific remain. Both full repetitions about Abu Bakr’s weeping and the suggestion to have ‘Umar lead are retained, followed by Hafsah’s action, Stop, the emphatic reply and Hafsah’s final words. The historical print addresses two women in the last command, while the selected digital and modern print use the plural; the wording is not harmonized.

segments.arabic: [648] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أنس بن مالك الأنصارى وكان تبع النبي ﷺ وخدمه وصحبه
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari informed me—he had followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, served him and kept his company:

segments.arabic: أن أبا بكر كان يصلي لهم في وجع النبي ﷺ الذي توفي فيه حتى إذا كان يوم الإثنين وهم صفوف في الصلاة فكشف النبي ﷺ ستر الحجرة ينظر إلينا وهو قائم كأن وجهه ورقة مصحف ثم تبسم يضحك فهممنا أن نفتتن من الفرح برؤية النبي ﷺ فنكص أبو بكر على عقبيه ليصل الصف وظن أن النبي ﷺ خارج إلى الصلاة فأشار إلينا النبي ﷺ أن أتموا صلاتكم وأرخى الستر فتوفي من يومه
segments.english: That Abu Bakr used to lead them in prayer during the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in which he died. Then, on Monday, while they were in rows in prayer, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew back the curtain of the room and looked towards us while standing. His face was like a page of a copy of the Qur’an. Then he smiled, laughing. We almost became distracted by the joy of seeing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr stepped backwards to join the row, thinking that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was coming out to prayer. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to us to complete our prayer and let the curtain fall. He died that day.

notes: Anas’s following, serving and accompanying the Prophet remain in the complete chain. Monday, the prayer rows, standing at the curtain, the page-of-a-Qur’an comparison, smiling, near distraction through joy, Abu Bakr stepping back, the gesture to finish and death that day remain. All six selected honorifics are preserved; the historical print adds a final honorific absent from the selected digital and modern readings. No historical calendar date or explanatory brightness clause is inserted.

segments.arabic: [649] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز عن أنس قال
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: لم يخرج النبي ﷺ ثلاثا فأقيمت الصلاة فذهب أبو بكر يتقدم، فقال نبي الله ﷺ بالحجاب فرفعه فلما وضح وجه النبي ﷺ ما نظرنا منظرا كان أعجب إلينا من وجه النبي ﷺ حين وضح لنا فأومأ النبي ﷺ بيده إلى أبي بكر أن يتقدم وأرخى النبي ﷺ الحجاب فلم يقدر عليه حتى مات
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not come out for three days. The iqamah was given, and Abu Bakr went forward. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the curtain and lifted it. When the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, appeared, we had never seen a sight more pleasing to us than the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it appeared to us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured with his hand to Abu Bakr to go forward. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, let the curtain fall, and he could not be reached until he died.

notes: The full Abu Ma‘mar/‘Abd al-Warith/‘Abd al-‘Aziz/Anas chain, three days, movement forward, lifting the curtain, repeated face description, hand gesture and lowering of the curtain remain. All six selected honorifics remain, although Bewley condenses the repeated face description. The selected فلم يقدر عليه is rendered could not be reached, following the passive vocalization in the modern print; the historical print has the first-person نقدر. Both English comparisons render this as not seeing him again. The difference is recorded rather than converting the selected passive wording into a first-person statement.

segments.arabic: [650] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثنا ابن وهب قال: حدثني يونس عن ابن شهاب عن حمزة بن عبد الله أنه أخبره عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah ibn ‘Abd Allah, that he informed him from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: لما اشتد برسول الله ﷺ وجعه قيل له في الصلاة، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس قالت عائشة إن أبا بكر رجل رقيق إذا قرأ غلبه البكاء، فقال مروه فيصلي فعاودته قال مروه فيصلي إنكن صواحب يوسف
segments.english: When the pain of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, grew severe, prayer was mentioned to him. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. When he recites, weeping overcomes him.” He said: “Tell him, and let him pray.” She repeated it to him. He said: “Tell him, and let him pray. You are the women associated with Yusuf.”

segments.arabic: تابعه الزبيدي وابن أخي الزهري وإسحاق بن يحيى الكلبي عن الزهري، وقال عقيل ومعمر عن الزهري عن حمزة عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Al-Zubaydi, the nephew of al-Zuhri, and Ishaq ibn Yahya al-Kalbi corroborated it from al-Zuhri. And ‘Uqayl and Ma‘mar said: From al-Zuhri, from Hamzah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The first route retains Ibn Wahb related to us and Yunus related to me; the historical print instead uses Ibn Wahb related to me. Hamzah’s father remains unnamed. The full complaint, all three instructions and repetition remain. The final corroboration names all three transmitters from al-Zuhri; Bewley abbreviates this and Khan omits it. The additional ‘Uqayl/Ma‘mar route goes from Hamzah directly to the Prophet in the selected source, without the father; the missing intermediary is not silently supplied. Both source honorifics remain.
